title: Beyond Successful Play: Diagnosing Opponent Modeling in Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.17310v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Language-model agents are expected to adapt to others whose behavior changes through interaction. Yet adaptation may rely on learned behavioral patterns rather than theory of mind (ToM): the ability to infer others' mental states, including beliefs and intentions. We introduce a benchmark and diagnostic framework for repeated hide-and-seek against algorithmic opponents with explicitly defined recursive belief updates. Their ground-truth beliefs and action probabilities let us distinguish adaptive play, action prediction, and belief tracking through live interaction, fixed-history evaluation, and controlled information interventions. With structured elicitation and behavioral supervised fine-tuning (SFT), we find improved play in several tested settings, but diagnostics reveal limitations in opponent prediction and belief tracking. We test whether supervising opponent action probabilities can address this predictive deficit in Qwen2.5-7B-

translated_title: 超越成功对局：诊断大语言模型中的对手建模能力
translated_abstract: 语言模型智能体被期望能够适应那些行为会随交互而改变的其他参与者。然而，这种适应可能依赖于学习到的行为模式，而非心智理论——即推断他人心理状态（包括信念和意图）的能力。我们提出了一个基准与诊断框架，通过与具有明确定义的递归信念更新机制的算法对手进行重复的捉迷藏博弈来进行评估。由于这些对手的真实信念和动作概率是已知的，我们能够通过实时交互、固定历史评估和受控信息干预，将适应性对局、动作预测和信念追踪区分开来。借助结构化引导和行为监督微调（SFT），我们发现在多个测试场景中对局表现有所提升，但诊断结果显示模型在对手预测和信念追踪方面存在局限。我们进一步测试了监督对手动作概率能否解决Qwen2.5-7B中的这一预测缺陷。
tldr: 该论文提出了一个基于重复捉迷藏博弈的基准与诊断框架，揭示大语言模型虽能通过行为SFT提升对局表现，但在对手动作预测和信念追踪方面仍存在缺陷，表明其适应能力更多源于习得的行为模式而非真正的心智理论。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a repeated hide-and-seek benchmark and diagnostic framework revealing that LLMs improve play with behavioral SFT but still show deficits in opponent prediction and belief tracking, indicating their adaptation relies on learned behavioral patterns rather than genuine theory of mind.
